activity_context.topic_title: Mean and Variance of the Normal Distribution

feedback.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(-1,{\sigma }^{2})$ and $P(X>1)=0.0618,$ use the table to find $\sigma ,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.4\,$ | $\,0.9251\,$ | $\,0.9265\,$ | $\,0.9279\,$ |
| $\,1.5\,$ | $\,0.9382\,$ | $\,0.9394\,$ | $\,0.9406\,$ |
| $\,1.6\,$ | $\,0.9495\,$ | $\,0.9505\,$ | $\,0.9515\,$ |

$\sigma ≈$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we convert the given probability into a cumulative probability using the complement:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 1) & =1-P(X>1) \\  & =1-0.0618 \\  & =0.9382\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 1) & =0.9382 \\ P\,(Z\le \frac{1-(-1)}{\sigma }) & =0.9382 \\ Φ\,(\frac{2}{\sigma }) & =0.9382 \\ \frac{2}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.9382)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(1.54)=0.9382\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.9382)=1.54.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sigma } & =1.54 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{2}{1.54} \\ \sigma  & ≈1.30,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
